newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Golden Vale says H2 outlook promising.
newsitem.headline: Golden Vale says H2 outlook promising.

text.p: Irish food group Golden Vale Plc said on Tuesday that the outlook for the second half of the year was promising despite tough market conditions in some sectors.
"The continuing task is to improve group competitiveness through cost base reductions and increased focus on consumer needs," the company said in a half-year results statement.
It announced a 59 percent increase in pre-tax profit for the year ended June 30, 1997 to 6.5 million punts.

"The results for the first half year are encouraging in overall terms and particularly the strong growth in processed cheese sales volumes and profitability, the improved performance of GV Holland and the strong cash generation achieved," managing director Jim Walsh said.

Golden Vale said turnover slipped by 3.8 percent to 278 million Irish pounds but this was entirely due to lower volumes and prices for butter and milk powders and was partially offset by gains in cheese and other businesses.
The butter and milk powders division, which saw margins remain tight, accounted for 41 percent of sales in the first half of 1997 against 46 percent in 1996.

The division recorded an operating profit of 2.1 million against 1.9 million in the first half of 1996 while profits from the cheese business were 2.0 million after a loss of 0.3 million a year earlier.
Golden Vale's other businesses, which include its activities in fluid milks, agri-trading, spreads and cream liqueurs, reported operating profits of 4.2 million against 4.1 million a year earlier.
Golden Vale said the overall margin on sales increased to three percent from two percent.
Looking ahead, Golden Vale said it planned to grow as a broad-based food company.
"This will mean continued investment in existing growth markets together with acquisitions, where appropriate, to strengthen group market position," it said.
